definitions.gloss: misunderstanding; wrong idea; misconception; mistaken belief
definitions.explanation: A fundamental error in one's understanding of a situation, role, or appropriate behavior, often implying that the person's attitude or thinking is misguided.

examples.japanese: それは{心得違|こころえちが}いだ。
{心得違|こころえちが}いをしていたようだ。
examples.english: It seems I had the wrong idea.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{立場|たちば}を{忘|わす}れるとは、とんだ{心得違|こころえちが}いだ。
examples.english: Forgetting your position — what a gross misconception.

notes:
A compound of {心得|こころえ} (understanding, knowledge) and {違|ちが}い (difference, mistake). Implies that someone has a fundamentally mistaken understanding of a situation, their role, or appropriate behavior. Often carries a tone of reprimand — pointing out that someone's thinking or attitude is wrong.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {心得違|こころえちが}いをする: to be mistaken, to have the wrong idea
- {心得違|こころえちが}いも{甚|はなは}だしい: a gross misconception
- とんだ{心得違|こころえちが}い: a serious misunderstanding

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {勘違|かんちが}い: misunderstanding — more common in everyday speech; simpler factual mistakes
- {思|おも}い{違|ちが}い: wrong impression — gentler; focuses on incorrect assumptions
- {誤解|ごかい}: misunderstanding — neutral; can refer to any kind of misinterpretation
